sources.observation: The university teaching protocol specifies 1 mol/L NaOH and 0.1 mol/L copper sulfate, then 1 mL alkali and ten drops of copper reagent. It describes a transient blue precipitate and a violet protein result after mixing. This supports recipe plausibility; a school adaptation still needs its own supervised controls.

The page uses a prepared ethanolic ninhydrin reagent on glycine-bearing filter paper. Its preparation and hazard table disagree on reagent concentration. The supplied task avoids unreviewed student reagent preparation, uses released reagent and drying before supervised heating; no original one-to-one protocol identity is claimed.
